newsitem.title: UK: Copper spikes on options, covering, thin volumes.
newsitem.headline: Copper spikes on options, covering, thin volumes.

text.p: The sharp rally in copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) early on Monday was sparked by options exposure and extended by short covering and a lack of liquidity in underlying futures, traders said.
Three month copper futures raced to a 2-1/2 month high of $2,165 a tonne on the pre-market on Monday, up $126 from Friday's afternoon close and $206 up on Thursday's finish.
With the September/three months backwardation indicated at between $50 and $60, September copper values surged through two key upside option strike prices at $2,100 and $2,200.
Market makers short of these calls had to hedge against them as the market rose, prompting bouts of covering from short position holders on the futures market, dealers explained.
"There has been consistent fund short-covering from that point (around $2,050) on," said one fund player.
The effect of options covering was heightened by the fact that September options go off the board on Wednesday.
"The options definitely started the ball rolling this morning," said one options dealer. "Anything above $2,000 would have been given a zero delta until late last week."
"But the overall market was very short as well," he added.
"The lack of liquidity in underlying futures is a problem again," another options trader said.
"The market raced through two key strikes without touching the sides, but you could hardly buy copper," he added.

As at the close of trade last Thursday, open interest on $2,000 September call options was 1,525 lots (equivalent to 38,125 tonnes). At $2,100 it was bigger at 2,239 lots (55,975 tonnes) and at $2,200 a more modest 1,050 lots (26,250 tonnes).
Options traders were also frustrated by low volumes on the options market.
Some dealers trying to buy calls on nearby months as a cover against the spike in prices said they had to search hard for sellers, even though volatilities were marked sharply higher.
"I traded October at 32 percent (volatility) this morning, but there are very few sellers of options out there," said one.
October was at around 22.5 percent volatility last Tuesday.

Dealers said conditions could remain volatile up to and just following the September options declaration at 1030 GMT on Wednesday. If values started to ease, the selling could gather pace as options dealers unwound their hedges, traders warned.
But some were punting for higher numbers.
"You may see a small setback from the highs, but overall the charts point to $2,300," said one dealer.
Adding to nervousness and fuelling technical tightness were bullish fundamental developments in recent weeks.
Damage to the small Tsumeb copper smelter in Namibia means it will be out of operation for several weeks. And miners went on strike on Friday at Codelco's Salvador mine in Chile.
There is also nervousness over the outcome of labour talks at Phelps Dodge's Chino copper mine.
But while the ingredients are in place for further short term rallies, some analysts said the overall trend was down.

"This looks like a rally for the traders, I do not think it presages a reversal of the fundamentally weak medium to long term copper market outlook," said Nick Moore of the Flemings Global Mining Group.
At 1000 GMT, Three months copper had retreated from the highs to $2,100/10. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
